post.description:
Add originals to a published, admin-reviewed replication or reproduction:
a new record each, validated under this admin's name. All or none.

Move a record back to need_review for further scrutiny: one awaiting
approval, or one validated without an admin (an auto-validation rule). That one
leaves the validated table until an admin decides it, and its Source Records
row is marked deleted at commit (retire_validated_source_row), so it stops
feeding FLoRA.
Save or update a persistent admin note on an entry. Visible to all admins.

Confirm that both validators were right: this original was not replicated.

The record is rejected, so nothing is published for it. Its siblings are separate
records and are not touched. Originals an admin added to it would leave with it,
so they have to be removed first: this is refused while one is live.

Take an entry out of validation before its validators have decided it.

The scope says why, and so what happens next:
- wrong_original: this pair only. The import re-opens it when the extractor ships
  a different original at the same work and rank (csv_to_db).
- duplicate: this pair only, for good: the correct pair is already in FLoRA.
- not_replication: the whole article. Every other pair of the same replication
  paper that is still open is withdrawn with it; those decided or waiting for an
  admin are left as they are and returned for review. One blocked pair refuses
  the whole request, so nothing is withdrawn in part.

Each withdrawn record is rejected, so it is neither served nor published, and its
open assignment and unanswered slots close. Judgements already submitted stay, with
their points, as for any other rejection. The reason goes at the head of the admin
note; the note already there is kept below it.

get.description:

The complete file is the stored dataset in flora_data: the flora.csv the last

post.description:
Settle a clash between duplicate source rows (the FLoRA tab's Conflicts): the
outcome shown is confirmed, or another of the outcomes they gave chosen. A logged
change, with an optional note.

Put a FLoRA record back as it was right after one change in its log. The
restore is logged as a change itself, so it can be undone the same way.

Change a FLoRA record between replication and reproduction, with what the new
type's outcome is, as one logged change. It keeps its permanent id, and a restore
undoes it. The source records it derives from are not changed.

Send another admin a fresh invitation or recovery link.

An account that has never had a password gets an invitation; one that has
gets a recovery link. Either replaces the outstanding link of that kind.

The link goes to the address on file. A trusted admin cannot redirect it to
another mailbox, or they could take over any account by resetting its
password from an inbox they control. Only an account with no address yet
may be sent one at an address the caller types, and that address is not
recorded here: it is written to the account only when the link is redeemed,
which is the first proof that the address reaches its owner. Until then a
typo is corrected simply by sending again.

post.description:
Sign in with a handle and the email address on that account.

DELIBERATE PRODUCT DECISION, recorded so it is not mistaken for an
oversight: the account owner is NOT asked to prove they hold the mailbox.
Handle plus email is enough, and the email that follows is a notice after
the fact. Handles are public on the leaderboard and academic addresses are
often guessable, so anyone who knows both can obtain a real session for
that validator. See docs/PROJECT.md section 19.

Both values must still match the same account, so a wrong pairing is
refused rather than silently creating a duplicate.

One-time migration for an account created before email sign-in.

The personal code is that account's existing credential, so presenting it is
how its owner proves the account is theirs. Once an address is attached the
code is cleared: keeping both would leave the weaker of the two as a
permanent second way in.

Only accounts with no email can be claimed. Without that restriction this
would be a takeover path — knowing somebody's code would let an attacker
point their account at a new mailbox.
End this session. Idempotent, and never reveals whether one existed.

post.description:
Batch-claim pairs for the client prefetch buffer, within a serving mode.
Default: first pair is the active (started) one — a resumed pair if the
validator already has one *in this mode*, else a freshly started claim —
and the rest are buffered. buffered_only=True returns only buffered top-ups.
Promote a buffered slot to the active 'started' pair (5-day lock).
Reserve this validator's open records for a paper and return the coded set.
Renew an open table's holds and say which records this validator still holds.

Hard-mode validator can't access the article → flag the record for the
admin restricted-access queue and release their slot. No points awarded.

Senior validators (tier >= 2) can immediately reject a record as not a replication
without waiting for a second validator or LLM.

Consume a server-issued capability and release exactly its failed slot.

This path is intentionally separate from /api/skip: it writes no skip event,
does not increment skipped_count, and accepts no client-supplied identity.
The random stamp is the scoped capability and is useful only once.
